Beer · Briefs for a brewer

Built for the table.

Beer designed to meet the food: crisp enough to cool the heat, round enough to hold a char. Nothing has been brewed. Each beer is a brief for a head brewer to critique, change, or reject.

NASHA is in development. There is no brewery, no restaurant, no truck and no menu for sale yet. Images are concept visualizations and illustrations, not photographs of NASHA. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age. Any future beer sales depend on licences we have not yet obtained.

The Two-Pour ritual

One dish. Two beers.

A proposed way to eat: the same dish after two different pours. It is a design idea to test in tastings.

  1. 1

    Beer one

    A cold, clean Mexican-Style Lager arrives first, as designed.

  2. 2

    The dish

    Chicken 65 Totopos, a designed Chennai-style bar snack with masa chips.

  3. 3

    Beer two

    Then a Hefeweizen alongside the same dish, as designed.

How the experience might change: the same bite, tasted after two different beers. That is a hypothesis for a tasting, not a result. No guest has tried it, and no beer has been brewed.

Brewery vision

The brewery in plain sight.

The imagined brewhouse sits behind glass so guests can see the work. The equipment in this picture is illustrative: the vessel size and count are an open decision and nothing here fixes them.

Honest status

Not brewed yet.

No beer exists. There is no brewer on the team, no recipe and no licence. The first beers, if any, would likely be made with a partner brewery under rules we are still learning. Follow the path in Labs.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development.

The name was chosen by the founder. Legal clearance of the name is pending. Nothing here claims trademark ownership. There is no brewery, restaurant or truck open, and nothing is for sale. No site has been chosen.

In Hindi and Urdu, nasha means intoxication or addiction. We chose it for the feeling of being captivated by food and beer. We take that meaning seriously and will never present excess or addiction as something to admire. Cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Images show a possible future. The photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited, and the drawings are illustrations. They are not photographs of NASHA, of its food, or of its beer. About these images.

Menu items are designs for testing, not served food. Heat and vegetarian labels describe how a dish is designed, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.

The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, set in a standard font. It is not a logo, not an official brand mark, and no trademark is claimed. No logo has been approved or released.
